findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition shadows 4-arg version
findings.body: app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: once as (from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again as (from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first, so any existing caller using the 4-argument max_width/max_height form will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). This silently breaks backward compatibility while adding the new 3-argument form used for percentage downsizing.

findings.title: Loop checks tempfile.size instead of path size, never sees shrink
findings.body: In UploadsController#create_upload the retry loop checks tempfile.size while OptimizedImage.downsize overwrites tempfile.path in place via an external convert process. tempfile.size stats the open file descriptor, which still points to the old inode if the converter unlinks/recreates the path, so the size appears unchanged. The loop then always runs all 5 iterations and shrinks an image to ~0.8^5 (~33%) even when one pass would have sufficed. Use File.size(tempfile.path) to stat the path.

findings.title: In-place downsize with unchecked return risks data loss
findings.body: UploadsController calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) using the same file as source and destination and never checks the return value. If convert/gifsicle fails it can truncate or corrupt the only copy of the upload, and the code retries the same failing command up to 5 times then proceeds to create the Upload from the corrupted/oversized file. Use a separate temp destination and abort/handle error if downsize returns false.

findings.title: Animated downsize passes percentage to gifsicle resize-fit
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize_instructions_animated just delegates to resize_instructions_animated, which builds gifsicle --resize-fit <dimensions>. The new upload flow passes "80%" as dimensions. gifsicle expects WxH for --resize-fit, not a percentage, so animated GIF downsizing will fail, return false, and large GIFs will never be reduced to SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.

findings.title: Remote download hardcodes 10MB ignoring site settings
findings.body: FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes. Admins who configured a larger max_image_size_kb will have valid remote images rejected/truncated at 10MB, and the limit no longer tracks configuration. The cap should derive from site settings, e.g. max of image/attachment limits.

findings.title: Client validation hardcodes 10MB and ignores type setting
findings.body: validateUploadedFile replaced Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] with hardcoded 10*1024. This ignores both max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb and breaks admins who raise limits above 10MB (client rejects files server would accept) or lower attachment limits below 10MB (client allows files server will reject). Keep per-type site-setting lookup; if large images are to be downsized server-side the image limit needs explicit handling, not a global hardcode.

findings.title: 413 error message hardcodes 10MB
findings.body: displayErrorForUpload for HTTP 413 replaced Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024. The alerted max_size_kb will be wrong whenever the configured limit differs from 10MB, and it always reports the image limit even for attachment uploads. Read the message value from site settings.
